correctness.rationale: For exactly k surviving pollinators, each survivor set has weight (1-q)^k q^(b-k); the corresponding coefficient sum is A_k, or A_k divided by the positive binomial(b,k) in the normalized Bernstein basis. Exhausted all ordered guild sizes through eight by enumerating row multisets and recovering the labeled counts by multinomial weights. Tested connectivity by closure on intersecting neighborhoods. For each survivor mask, independently propagated the sets of plants that can be injectively assigned to surviving pollinators, processing pollinators rather than using the source's plant-first recurrence. The 70492 labeled matrices yield 21 same-signature comparisons between distinct coefficient vectors, all componentwise comparable. The connected degree-matched witnesses have vectors (0,5,19,27,17,4) and (0,5,20,26,14,3). Their difference factors as (1-q)^2(1-2q^2), with the claimed interior sign reversal and endpoint orientation. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/audit_pollinators.py capacity.
residual_risks: The proof of comparability is a complete finite computation, not a general characterization of stochastic matching ranks.

value.rationale: The finding locates the first network size at which two margins do not control even the ordering of expected optimal service across failure rates. Below that size it provides the stronger discrete survivor-layer order. The witness distinguishes robustness under independent losses from the established observation that equal degrees need not fix static maximum matching.
residual_risks: The one-to-one service and cost-free reallocation assumptions are modeling idealizations; no inference about real pollination or correlated failure follows.
